title: Monday, ten past eight: 'I have called y'all three times this morning'
purpose: Story S3, before the fix. One advisor is at the counter until nine and the phones ring out; this caller got through on her fourth try. Travis says why, handles a flashing check engine light properly and books her for nine. Her doubt, whether she will ever reach the shop again, gets an apology and no more.

call.day: the Monday of week T-6, 08:10 (rule R6; card S03, call 31)
call.note: Her calls at 07:34, 07:46 and 07:58 rang out; this one was answered on the second ring stage. The three misses are resolved by this call as got_through.

scenario.who_calls: A first-time caller, Tamika Ellison, in the car park at her work, on her fourth call of the morning.
scenario.job: check engine light flashing with a shake: diagnose a misfire
scenario.wants: somebody to answer; then to know whether she can drive it and what it costs to look at
scenario.what_happens: Travis apologises and says why the phones rang out, establishes that the light is flashing and the car shakes all the time, tells her to keep off the interstate, offers nine o'clock with the diagnostic technician, gives the price out the door with what it usually finds, answers her doubt with an apology, takes her name and number and reads the number back, books and sums up.

script.said: Brennan Auto Care, this is Travis.
Finally. I have called y'all three times this mornin'.
I'm sorry about that. Monday mornings we're three deep at the counter and it's just me up here till nine. I've got you now. What's going on?
My check engine light's flashin' and the whole car is shakin'. It started on the way to work.
Okay. Flashing, not just on?
Flashin'. On and off.
Okay. That's a misfire, and that's the one light I don't want you driving on. Where are you right now?
I'm in the parkin' lot at work. Off Amnicola.
Okay, that's not far. What kind of car?
Twenty-seventeen Elantra.
And is it shaking all the time, or just when you give it gas?
All the time. It's worse at a red light.
Okay. Here's what I'd do. Don't take it on the interstate. If you can limp it over here, slow, I can have Kevin — he's our diagnostic tech — on it at nine this morning.
Uh-huh.
What's it gonna cost me for him to look at it?

The diagnostic's one thirty-five, and out the door with tax that's one fifty-four eighty-six. Most times a misfire's a coil or a plug, and he finds it inside that hour. If it's more than that, I call you before we do anything. And like I said, I can get you in at nine.
Okay.
I mean, I about gave up and called somebody else. If I can't get y'all on the phone, how am I supposed to know when my car's done?
I hear you, and I'm sorry. Monday mornings get away from us.
...Okay. Well. I can be there by nine.
Good. What's your name?
Tamika Ellison.
Tamika, and a good number for you?
Four two three, five five five, oh one three seven.
Four two three, five five five, oh one three seven. Okay, Tamika. I've got you down for nine this morning, and I'll write it up myself.
Can somebody give me a ride back to work?
Yes ma'am, we'll run you back. So that's nine this morning, the Elantra, and Kevin's checking that misfire.
Okay. Thank you.
Thank you for sticking with us, Tamika. Drive it easy.
